readme:
## README.md
# Agricultural Commodity Probability Layers (`public-commodities`)

Spatially explicit probability layers for tropical agricultural commodities linked to
deforestation risk — *where a given commodity is likely to be grown*, at high spatial
resolution. Intended for commodity-driven deforestation analysis, supply-chain due
diligence, and conservation prioritization.

**Base URL**: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/`
**STAC**: [`stac-collection.json`](https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/stac-collection.json)

> ⚠️ **These layers are model output, not observed ground truth.** Values are
> probabilities in `[0, 1]` — never areas, yields, or production volumes — and they
> must **never be summed**. Read the caveats before drawing conclusions about any
> individual location.

---

## Datasets

| Collection | Commodity | Extent | Year | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`fdap-2025b-cocoa-peru-2024`](https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024/stac-collection.json) | Cocoa | Peru | 2024 | 10 m / H3 res 9 |

---

## Cocoa Probability, Peru 2024 (FDAP model 2025b)

Per-pixel probability that a 10 m pixel contains cocoa trees.

### Source & attribution

- **Producer**: Forest Data Partnership (FDAP) — produced by Google
- **Upstream asset**: Earth Engine `projects/forestdatapartnership/assets/cocoa/model_2025b`,
  band `probability` ([catalog page](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_forestdatapartnership_assets_cocoa_model_2025b))
- **Model**: machine learning over AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings; the
  upstream collection is pan-tropical (−24° to +24° latitude), yearly, 2020–2024
- **License**: **CC-BY-4.0**
- **Required attribution**: *"Produced by Google for the Forest Data Partnership"*
- **Citation**: Forest Data Partnership. 2026. *Community models 2025b.*
  <https://github.com/google/forest-data-partnership/tree/main/models/model_2025b/README.md>

> Note the version distinction: FDAP **2025a** is CC-BY-**NC**-4.0 (non-commercial,
> with separate commercial terms). This dataset is **2025b**, which is plain
> CC-BY-4.0. Do not carry the 2025a NC clause over to this layer, or vice versa.

### How this extract was made

The upstream yearly image was filtered to 2024, `.mosaic()`-ed, and clipped to the
FAO GAUL 2015 level-0 boundary for Peru (`FAO/GAUL_SIMPLIFIED_500m/2015/level0`,
`ADM0_NAME = 'Peru'`), then exported at **native 10 m** in EPSG:4326 and republished
as a COG plus H3 hexagonal parquet. No resampling or rescaling was applied.

### Assets

| Asset | Format | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `cocoa-peru-2024-cog` | Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, Float32, EPSG:4326 | [`fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024-cog.tif`](https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024-cog.tif) |
| `cocoa-peru-2024-hex` | H3 parquet, res 9, hive-partitioned by `h0` | `fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |

**COG**: 140,824 × 204,174 px at 0.000089831528412° (~10 m), DEFLATE, 5 overview
levels, 64.67 GB. Band 1 = `probability`.

**Hex**: 10,768,450 rows across 4 `h0` partitions (Peru spans 4 H3 base cells).
Columns: `probability` (double), `h9`, `h8`, `h0` (uint64). Native resolution **9**,
with `h8` — the catalog's universal join key — and `h0` as parent columns.

Reduced with the **`mean`** reducer: each cell holds the *area-weighted mean* of the
source pixel probabilities, which is the correct reduction for an intensity. Only
cells containing at least one valid pixel are written, so coverage is sparse and
follows the Peru boundary rather than filling the base cells.

### ⚠️ NoData

Outside-Peru pixels are Float32 **NaN**, and **the COG carries no tagged nodata value
in its header**. Any tool reading this raster must treat NaN as nodata explicitly
rather than relying on the header. (The hex build passes `--nodata nan` for exactly
this reason; without it, the masked area leaks in as valid data.)

### ⚠️ Interpretation caveats

From the FDAP model documentation — these matter:

- Accuracy figures computed from *generated* evaluation data are **overestimates**
  relative to independent validation data.
- The cocoa model **over-predicts in ecotones** (transition zones between vegetation
  types).
- The training set is **largely opportunistic** and does not comprehensively
  represent every class in every region.
- Values are **not stable between years** — do not difference this 2024 layer against
  another year to infer change.

Cocoa is sparse in Peru: mean probability across all cells is only **~0.0042**, with a
maximum of **0.9988**. A linear 0–1 color ramp will therefore look almost entirely
empty; rescale to a narrow low range, or threshold, to see structure.

Treat the layer as a **screening and prioritization aid**, not as ground truth for any
individual parcel.

---

## Querying the hex layer (DuckDB)

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

-- Overall distribution (note: AVG/MAX, never SUM — probability is not extensive)
SELECT COUNT(*)      AS cells,
       AVG(probability) AS mean_p,
       MAX(probability) AS max_p
FROM read_parquet(
  'https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet',
  hive_partitioning = true
);
```

```sql
-- Likely cocoa areas, rolled up to the h8 join resolution
SELECT h8, AVG(probability) AS mean_p, COUNT(*) AS h9_cells
FROM read_parquet(
  'https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet',
  hive_partitioning = true
)
GROUP BY h8
HAVING AVG(probability) > 0.25
ORDER BY mean_p DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

```sql
-- Read a single base cell only (partition pruning keeps this cheap)
SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(probability)
FROM read_parquet(
  'https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet',
  hive_partitioning = true
)
WHERE h0 = 578994027093819391;
```

**Aggregation rule**: `probability` is a unitless intensity. Use `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`.
Rolling up to a coarser resolution means `GROUP BY h8` with `AVG` — **never** `SUM`.

To join against another catalog dataset, join on `h8` (both sides physically carry
it), not on the finest column.

## Displaying the COG (MapLibre GL JS + titiler)

The raster is served as web tiles by the catalog's titiler instance. There is no
PMTiles / vector-tile asset for this dataset — it is a raster, so there is no
`source-layer` to set.

```js
const COG = 'https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-commodities/fdap-2025b/cocoa-peru-2024-cog.tif';

const map = new maplibregl.Map({
  container: 'map',
  style: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json',
  center: [-75, -9],   // Peru
  zoom: 5
});

map.on('load', () => {
  map.addSource('cocoa', {
    type: 'raster',
    tiles: [
      'https://titiler.nrp-nautilus.io/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.png' +
      `?url=${encodeURIComponent(COG)}` +
      '&colormap_name=greens' +
      '&rescale=0,0.3'      // NOT 0,1 — cocoa is sparse; 0-1 renders nearly blank
    ],
    tileSize: 256
  });
  map.addLayer({
    id: 'cocoa-layer',
    type: 'raster',
    source: 'cocoa',
    paint: { 'raster-opacity': 0.8 }
  });
});
```
